card.title: German

heading: Learn German, from first words to C1.
lead: A complete course in the standard German of Germany. Articles and gender, the four cases, adjective endings, verb-second and verb-last word order, Konjunktiv II and the passive are each explained directly before you practise them, and the last tier covers nominal style, modal particles, spoken German and German in Austria and Switzerland.
fineprint: The whole course is free: all 76 modules, the grammar reference, word practice and the placement test. Specializations, stories, conversation practice, DTZ, Goethe, telc and TestDaF practice papers and the other extras are part of Premium, €8.99 a month or €69.99 a year.

panel.label: The course: eight tiers, 76 modules

items.title: Tier 1 · Sounds and first words
items.text: Pronunciation and spelling, greetings, nouns and articles, sein, numbers.

items.title: Tier 2 · Everyday basics
items.text: The present tense, haben, plurals, word order, negation.

items.title: Tier 3 · Daily life
items.text: Modal and separable verbs, the accusative and dative, prepositions.

items.title: Tier 4 · The past
items.text: The perfect tense, two-way prepositions, the imperative, reflexive verbs.

items.title: Tier 5 · Building fluency
items.text: Subordinate clauses, adjective endings, the preterite, the future, the genitive.

items.title: Tier 6 · Intermediate
items.text: Konjunktiv II, conditions, relative and infinitive clauses, the passive.

items.title: Tier 7 · Upper intermediate
items.text: The passive in all tenses, reported speech, connectors, word formation.

items.title: Tier 8 · Advanced
items.text: Nominal style, modal particles, register, spoken German, varieties of German.

panel.note: Tiers 1–2 are A1, Tier 3 A1–A2, Tier 4 A2, Tier 5 B1, Tier 6 B1–B2, Tier 7 B2 and Tier 8 C1.

sections.heading: German grammar explained, not guessed at

items.title: Cases and endings one step at a time
items.text: The accusative, the dative, the genitive and the prepositions that take them each have their own module, and adjective endings are split in two: after the definite article, then after the indefinite article and with no article.

items.title: Word order as a rule
items.text: The verb in second place, the verb at the end of a subordinate clause and separable prefixes at the end of the sentence are taught as rules with examples, so a sentence like Ich rufe dich morgen an has a reason behind it.

items.title: Up to the German of real texts
items.text: Tiers 7 and 8 cover reported speech, Amtsdeutsch (the German of forms and authorities), nominal style, participle phrases and modal particles such as doch and mal, and a module on German in Austria and Switzerland.

items.title: Feedback that says why
items.text: Every answer gets feedback with a reason and a link to the grammar rule. A translation worded differently from the expected answer can still be accepted.

items.title: Every word inspectable
items.text: Tap any German word in a module, a story or a practice paper for its gender, meaning, forms and audio.

items.title: Speaking with pronunciation feedback
items.text: Speaking exercises in the modules are assessed for pronunciation, and 12 sets of common traps cover false friends and the mistakes English speakers make with word order and prepositions.

sections.heading: Practice papers for DTZ, Goethe, telc and TestDaF
sections.intro: The course has two timed practice papers for each of these exams, with original texts and recordings, covering reading, listening and writing. They have no speaking part and cannot tell you which result you would get; the German exams page says what they cover and where they differ from the real exams.
items: DTZ (Deutsch-Test für Zuwanderer), the final test of the integration course in Germany, with a result of A2 or B1.
Goethe-Zertifikat: A1 (Start Deutsch 1), A2, B1, B2, C1 and C2 (Großes Deutsches Sprachdiplom).
telc Deutsch: A1 (Start Deutsch 1), A2 (Start Deutsch 2), B1 (Zertifikat Deutsch), B2, C1, C1 Hochschule and C2.
TestDaF, the test for studying at a German university.

sections.heading: German for your field
sections.intro: Thirteen specialization courses, each with nine modules in three stages: Foundations written for learners at Tier 4, Working vocabulary at Tier 6, and Professional at Tier 8.

items.question: Is the German course really free?
items.answer: Yes. All 76 modules from A1 to C1, the grammar reference, word practice, the common traps and the placement test are free, with 5 Ask AI questions a day. Premium adds the extras listed above.

items.question: I already know some German. Do I have to start at the beginning?
items.answer: No. The placement test suggests where in the course to start.

items.question: Which German does it teach?
items.answer: The standard German of Germany. A Tier 8 module covers German in Austria and Switzerland, such as Grüß Gott, Jänner and the Swiss spelling without ß.

items.question: Can it prepare me for the Goethe, telc or TestDaF exam?
items.answer: The course goes up to C1, and Premium adds timed practice papers for 15 exams (DTZ, Goethe, telc and TestDaF), for reading, listening and writing. They cannot tell you whether you would pass or which result you would get. See the German exams page.

items.question: Is there a version for Russian or Finnish speakers?
items.answer: Yes. German for Russian speakers and German for Finnish speakers have the same tiers and exam papers, with explanations in Russian or Finnish and grammar compared with that language.
